page.title: Best Variable ND Filter for Video (2026): PolarPro vs K&F, Freewell, Tiffen, Hoya
page.h1: Best variable ND filter for video
page.desc: Which variable ND avoids the X pattern and yellow cast for video: PolarPro Edition II overall, K&F ND2-32 True Color under $110. Maker prices checked 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best variable ND filter for video is the PolarPro Peter McKinnon VND Edition II, 2-5 stop ($249.99 in 67 mm at polarpro.com, seen 2026-11-06): its preset 2-to-5-stop range cannot be turned into the X pattern, it clicks at every full stop, and PolarPro rates it vignette-free down to 16 mm. If you will not spend $250 on a filter, the K&F Concept ND2-32 True Color ({buy:kf-concept-nd2-32-true-color-vnd-67mm}) wins the under-$110 segment: 1 to 5 stops with built-in hard stops at both ends, a 28-layer coating, and a titanium True Color layer aimed at the yellow cast owners complain about most.

The X pattern is the top worry before buying. It appears near a variable ND's maximum setting, soonest on wide lenses, because the two polarizers cross. Both picks stop at 5 stops, so you cannot rotate into it. For brighter scenes, add a fixed ND rather than buying a 1-to-9-stop filter and running it near the end of its range.

The second complaint is color cast. In the two owner threads we counted, 4 of 10 and 4 of 11 posters reported a green or yellow shift from their VND. The PolarPro and K&F True Color both market neutral glass, and owner reports for both are mostly clean, but every VND shifts a little; set white balance with the filter on.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Color cast comes first. In one EOSHD thread on the best variable NDs, 4 of 10 posters reported a green or yellow tint, and in a second thread 4 of 11 did. Most said white balance fixes it, but it changes as you turn the ring on cheaper filters. The X pattern came up from 3 of 10 posters in the first thread and from almost every forum question we read; it shows at the dark end, on wide lenses first, and one poster called it unfixable in post. Next come sharpness loss at the darkest settings (2 posters), lens hoods and caps that no longer fit because the front ring is one size larger (2 posters), and the price of premium filters (2 posters called PolarPro's pricing marketing-driven). Nobody reported a ring coming loose.

Which one by need

  • Paid video work, any lens: PolarPro Edition II 2-5 stop. Click stops let you set exposure by feel, and the fixed range cannot cross-polarize. Add the 6-9 stop version for bright days.
  • Under $110, want hard stops and an ND2 setting: K&F ND2-32 True Color ({buy:kf-concept-nd2-32-true-color-vnd-67mm}). The ND2 start helps indoors and on overcast days at f/1.8, where a 2-stop minimum is already too dark. Buy the 77 mm version ({buy:kf-concept-nd2-32-true-color-vnd-77mm}) and step-up rings if you own several lenses.
  • Strict budget: K&F's plain Nano-Xcel ND2-32 (67 mm, $69.99 on kfconcept.com, 2026-11-06) has the same 1-5 stop range and hard stops without the True Color coating. It is the cheapest hard-stop VND we found.
  • One filter for photos and video, 2 to 8 stops: Tiffen Variable ND. Expect to back off from the 8-stop end on wide lenses.

Not recommended for video

Skip 1-to-9-stop filters (ND2-400 and ND2-2000 types) as your only ND for wide lenses; owners and K&F's own guide say the X arrives above about 7 stops at 16 to 24 mm. Skip VND plus polarizer combos unless you need the polarizer: a Reddit commenter ranked them below a plain VND of the same series for image quality, and a polarizer rotates the sky's brightness as you pan. One Reddit commenter also warned against K&F's lines other than Nano-X, which is why the picks above are Nano-X (sold as Nano-Xcel) filters.
